entities.name: PMID:25069624
observations: In isolated human RBCs, a natural histone mixture induced dose-dependent annexin-V-positive PS exposure; approximately 14% were positive at 20 μg/mL. Histone-treated RBCs increased prothrombin activation and accelerated fibrin formation in functional coagulation assays.
Histone H4 was the dominant active individual histone; heparin neutralization or activated-protein-C cleavage abolished PS exposure. Reversibility after washout was not established.

entities.name: PMID:31302949
observations: Extracellular histones induced dose-dependent annexin-V PS exposure and eryptosis in freshly isolated human RBCs within 3 hours, with calcium elevation, ROS, cell shrinkage, and caspase-3 activation.

No hemolysis or RBC-ghost calcein leakage was detected after 24 hours; heparin and anti-TLR2 partially inhibited the response. This study did not report a direct coagulation assay or identify the active histone subtype in the available evidence.

entities.name: Histone H4
observations: Histone H4 was the principal active individual histone tested for inducing PS exposure and calcium influx in isolated human RBCs in PMID:25069624.

entities.name: Human red blood cells
observations: Isolated human RBCs directly respond to extracellular histones with PS externalization; a histone mixture and H4 can produce a procoagulant phenotype in functional coagulation assays.
